title: Mark Zuckerberg sends controversial message on the future of jobs
excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg published a sprawling essay on Aug. 10, making his fullest case yet for where artificial intelligence is taking the economy. It was optimisti...
content_html:
Hillary Remy

Wed, August 12, 2026 at 2:33 PM PDT 5 min read

Mark Zuckerberg published a sprawling essay on Aug. 10, making his fullest case yet for where artificial intelligence is taking the economy. It was optimistic, occasionally philosophical, and clearly meant to set him apart from other AI executives who have spent the past year warning about mass job losses.

At 6,500 words, it read less like a corporate blog post and more like a manifesto aimed at reshaping how the public thinks about automation.

The pushback arrived almost immediately, and not from the direction anyone expected.

It did not come from rival CEOs or skeptical economists. It came from a fact-check sitting inside the recent history of Zuckerberg's own company. A few months old, it complicated the tidy story he was trying to tell.

Mark Zuckerberg says AI will create more jobs, not fewer, in 2026

In an essay titled "The Future Is for Everyone: The Path to a Positive AI Future," posted to Meta's website on Aug. 10, Zuckerberg pushed back against predictions of a job apocalypse.

He drew an implicit contrast with Anthropic's Dario Amodei, who has warned about potential job disruption from AI, though Zuckerberg did not name him directly.

"I do not understand why anyone who believes that AI will eliminate most jobs and much of humanity's relevance would rush to build that future," he wrote, according to Fortune.

  • Zuckerberg's stock rebound made him world's 5th richest at $222B

  • Mark Zuckerberg backs Elon Musk Silicon Valley decision

Zuckerberg, the world's sixth richest person with a net worth of $211 billion, argued that people will keep inventing new products and services and the jobs needed to build them, pointing to careers, like app developer and data-center operator, that barely existed a generation ago.

He expects new roles such as one-person studio designers, world builders creating virtual experiences, and personal biologists formulating individualized treatments.

Part of his optimism rests on a resource limit rather than a moral argument. Zuckerberg wrote that no matter how intelligent AI becomes, there will always be a finite amount of compute, creating an opportunity cost that makes inventing new things more valuable than simply automating jobs that already exist.

He also committed $115 million to America's Workforce Academy, a training program designed to prepare workers for data-center technician roles near Meta's facilities.

content_html_zh:
希拉里·雷米

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 12 日星期三下午 2:33 阅读 5 分钟

马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 于 8 月 10 日发表了一篇篇幅庞大的文章，对人工智能正在影响经济的方向提出了迄今为止最全面的论证。 这是乐观的，有时是哲学性的，显然是为了让他与其他人工智能高管区分开来，这些高管在过去的一年里一直在警告大规模失业。

它有 6,500 字，读起来不太像一篇企业博客文章，而更像是一份旨在重塑公众对自动化看法的宣言。

阻力几乎立刻就到来了，而且方向却出乎所有人的预料。

它并非来自竞争对手的首席执行官或持怀疑态度的经济学家。 它来自对扎克伯格自己公司近期历史的事实核查。 几个月前，这让他想要讲述的简洁故事变得复杂起来。

马克·扎克伯格表示，2026 年人工智能将创造更多而不是更少的就业机会

8 月 10 日，扎克伯格在 Meta 网站上发布了一篇题为“未来属于每个人：通向积极的人工智能未来之路”的文章，他反驳了有关就业灾难的预测。

他与 Anthropic 的达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 进行了含蓄的对比，后者曾警告人工智能可能会扰乱工作岗位，但扎克伯格没有直接提到他的名字。

据《财富》杂志报道，他写道：“我不明白为什么那些相信人工智能将消除大多数工作岗位和人类大部分相关性的人会急于建设这样的未来。”

更多马克·扎克伯格：

  • 微软首席执行官马克扎克伯格刚刚做出重大人工智能决策
  • 扎克伯格的股票反弹使他以 $222B 成为全球第五大富豪
  • 马克·扎克伯格支持埃隆·马斯克硅谷决定

扎克伯格是世界第六大富豪，净资产达 2110 亿美元，他认为人们将不断发明新产品和服务以及构建这些产品和服务所需的工作岗位，并指出了上一代人几乎不存在的职业，例如应用程序开发人员和数据中心运营商。

他期待新的角色，例如单人工作室设计师、创造虚拟体验的世界构建者以及制定个性化治疗的个人生物学家。

他的乐观情绪部分源于资源限制，而不是道德争论。 扎克伯格写道，无论人工智能变得多么智能，计算量总是有限的，从而产生了机会成本，使得发明新事物比简单地自动化现有工作更有价值。

他还向美国劳动力学院投入了 1.15 亿美元，这是一项培训计划，旨在帮助工人做好在 Meta 设施附近担任数据中心技术人员的准备。
